title: Integration of CT-based coronary angiography into the cardiac catheterization workflow: impact on intervention an outcomes
summary: The analyzed data from CT-based coronary angiography enable the treating physicians to better prepare the cardiac catheterization procedure and the subsequent treatment of stenoses. Currently, the data are evaluated in a standardized manner and reviewed by the examiner prior to the intervention in order to determine the further course of action. An extended analysis of the data can provide additional information for the procedure—for example, regarding the choice of catheter, stent, or the preparation of the stenoses. At present, however, neither the visualization of this extended analysis nor the display of CT images during cardiac catheterization - and thus their direct integration into the procedural workflow - is routinely performed. By additionally displaying the analyzed CT images during the procedure, we hope to further improve patient care.

interventions.name: The results of the CT coronary angiography are available during the invasive coronary angiography via an integrated display (intervention arm).
The investigator reviews the CT coronary angiography and its analysis prior to the invasive procedure (standard arm, corresponding to the routine approach according to internal SOPs).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Manifest coronary artery disease confirmed by CT coronary angiography with an indication for invasive coronary angiography
- CT coronary angiography and invasive coronary angiography performed at GRN Clinic Weinheim
- Capacity to provide informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients in whom, despite a positive CT angiography, no need for intervention is identified by invasive angiography or by coronary physiological assessment (iFR/RFR/FFR)
- Lack of informed consent from the participants
- Pregnant women, age < 18 years
